chapter: Los Angeles with Mutt Carey and the taxi dances
title: Mutt Carey as leader, rooming in Boyle Heights, and the Liberty Syncopators
summary: Tudie only fronted the One-Eleven Syncopators while Mutt truly led his band, ran marked-card poker games, and the band was called Papa Mutt's Liberty Syncopators.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: I want to ask you this. Talking to some of the older musicians out here, they say that the band Tudie had, the One-Eleven Band... That was the name of the band, wasn't it?
Yeah.
They say Tudie didn't lead...
The One-Eleven Syncopators.
Oh, that was it?
Mmm-hmm.
And that's the band that was playing a couple of blocks away from you?
Yeah, they played... The one that was upstairs... Well, most of the taxi dances was upstairs in some building.
What I wanted to ask you: I've heard a lot of people say that Tudie didn't really lead that band at all. He just was like a front man.
That's true.
Well, would you say that Mutt Carey led his band, or was he a front man?
Darensbourg - 147
No, no. Mutt Carey led the band. Absolutely.
And he'd knock off the numbers and tell you what to play and all this?

Oh yeah. Once in a while, we'd... Well, Mutt was one of them kind of...a con man himself. Papa... Frownin' George and Ram used to room with Papa Mutt. Papa Mutt was living out there in Boyle Heights. Because Papa Mutt married a Mexican woman, see, and all them Mexicans lived in Boyle Heights. I'll never forget... Some things I'll never forget. They lived on a little old street called Cheesebrough Lane, and Papa Mutt would say, "Well, we'll have a rehearsal, and I'm gonna have a pot of beans." And mostly he wanted to get us in a poker game. We were fairly young fools, and old Mutt had some marked cards -- and we'd lose all our money foolin' around there with Mutt, playing poker.
Did you rehearse with the band at all, or was it...?
Oh, we rehearsed a little.
Oh, when you said there was two tenors, do you mean one behind the other or two at one time?
No, just... Usually they had a team, alto and tenor.
Darensbourg - 148
I thought that's what you meant.
No, they had two tenors with an alto.
In those days, if you can remember that Liberty Dance Hall Band... What was the name of the band? What did it go under?
They went under Papa Mutt's Liberty Syncopators.
